title: An Agent-tool worker's prompt from brief ID names no turn cap it does not have
goal: compose_brief always fills the turn cap, so brief ID prints 'Your turn cap is N turns' for the kb-sprint skill's Agent-tool fallback, whose subagent has no --max-turns; brief gives the cap only when dispatch runs the session with one, and the role file's no-cap rule is the one an Agent-tool worker reads. Found by the SP-mujl7ebh review.

run:
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, os
tool = os.path.abspath("_tools/backlog.py")
tools = os.path.dirname(tool)
root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
def run(*a, prog=None):
    return subprocess.run(prog or [sys.executable, tool, "--root", root, *a], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
run(prog=["git", "init", "-q"])
iid = run("new", "story", "--title", "T", "--goal", "g", "--touch", "src/a.py").stdout.split()[2]
brief = run("brief", iid).stdout
sys.path.insert(0, tools)
os.chdir(root)
import bl_dispatch, bl_base
bl_base.load_settings(root)
text = bl_dispatch.compose_brief(bl_base.Backlog(root), iid, turns=77)
named_by_brief = "Your turn cap is" in brief
named_by_dispatch = "Your turn cap is 77 turns" in text
print("brief names a cap:", named_by_brief, "dispatch brief names 77:", named_by_dispatch, file=sys.stderr)
sys.exit(0 if (not named_by_brief and named_by_dispatch) else 1)
